campaign_record.title: Section 232 advanced-computing-chip tariff: a performance-threshold tax base, not a country tax base

occurrence.reference: Presidential Proclamation under Section 232 imposing a 25% ad valorem tariff on advanced computing chips, effective 2026-01-15; industry attack on the formula published 2026-08-27
occurrence.claim: A 25% Section 232 tariff took effect 2026-01-15 on logic integrated circuits under HTS 8471.50, 8471.80 and 8473.30 that cross defined Tensor Processing Performance and DRAM-bandwidth thresholds, with the White House fact sheet naming NVIDIA H200 and AMD MI325X as covered examples; by 2026-08-27 the AI industry was publicly attacking the threshold formula as taxing the wrong base.

occurrence_strength.basis: Dated and binding: a signed proclamation with an effective date (2026-01-15), named HTS subheadings, and a two-phase negotiation clock reporting by 2026-04-14 (White & Case client alert on the proclamation, https://www.whitecase.com/insight-alert/president-trump-orders-narrowly-targeted-25-section-232-tariff-certain-advanced). Second dated item: Ars Technica 2026-08-27 on the industry response.

economic_impact.basis: The tariff base is accelerator hardware inside the largest capex program in the market. It taxes the bill of materials of every US AI data center build, so the cost lands on hyperscaler capex and on anyone importing derivative products containing covered chips.

unmappedness.basis: The headline is fully covered. What is unmapped is the mechanism: a performance-THRESHOLD tariff creates a discontinuity that rewards designing just under the TPP and bandwidth lines, rewards domestic assembly and packaging of imported dies, and reprices tariff-engineering, customs classification and bonded-warehouse services. Nobody has mapped who gets paid for compliance and re-domiciling of the last assembly step.

public_market_reach.basis: Listed accelerator vendors, listed OSAT and packaging names, listed customs and logistics providers all sit on the chain. The choke question is whether the capture sits with listed OSAT or with private customs brokers, which a chain build would settle.

overlap.basis: Touches SIG-20260828-01 (AI infrastructure buildout) at the cost side, but that card's thesis is power and grid as the binding constraint. This is a tariff mechanism, a different link and a different clock. Does NOT restate TASTE-002: this is a dated US tariff instrument, not the Taiwan concentration-diversification macro story.

campaign_record.reason: Chain-worthy: a live, dated, binding trade instrument whose second-order consequences (threshold gaming, last-step assembly relocation, customs and classification services) are not in mainstream coverage. Held ALTERNATE pending Tally's money appraisal.

campaign_record.title: Polysilicon Section 232: the first minimum-import-price floor on solar, effective 2026-12-04

occurrence.reference: Presidential Proclamation of 2026-08-06 imposing a 15% ad valorem tariff plus a minimum import price program on polysilicon and derivative solar products, effective 2026-12-04
occurrence.claim: On 2026-08-06 a Section 232 proclamation imposed a 15% ad valorem tariff on downstream polysilicon derivatives (ingots, wafers, cells, modules) and, separately, minimum import prices of $21/kg for polysilicon, $100/kg for polysilicon ingots and wafers, $0.22/W for solar cells and $0.38/W for solar modules, taking effect 2026-12-04, with CBP requiring importers to certify compliant US sale prices or pre-2026-08-06 fixed-term contracts.

occurrence_strength.basis: A signed proclamation with a hard effective date, numeric price floors and a CBP certification regime. Second dated confirmation: Wiley alert on the same action, https://www.wiley.law/alert-Trump-Administration-Imposes-Section-232-Tariffs-and-Minimum-Import-Prices-on-Polysilicon-and-its-Derivatives.

economic_impact.basis: A price FLOOR, not just a tariff, sets a hard bottom on US module economics for every project financed after 2026-12-04. It resets utility-scale solar capex assumptions, PPA pricing and the domestic-content calculus in one instrument.

unmappedness.basis: Solar tariffs are a familiar story; a minimum-import-price regime is not. A price floor changes who captures margin in a way an ad valorem tariff does not: it protects the highest-cost domestic producer rather than penalising a country of origin, and it makes contract vintage (pre or post 2026-08-06) a balance-sheet fact. The chain from MIP to ingot and wafer capacity to module assembly to interconnection queue economics is essentially unwritten.

public_market_reach.basis: US polysilicon, wafer, cell and module producers are listed, as are the utility developers and the IPPs whose project returns move with the floor. Chinese producers who dominate the cost curve are mostly not reachable from a US brokerage account.

campaign_record.title: China's rare-earth export-control suspension expires 2026-11-10, with the magnet-technology decree behind it

occurrence.reference: MOFCOM Decrees 61 and 62 of 2025-10-09 on rare-earth items and rare-earth TECHNOLOGY, suspended from 2025-11-07 until 2026-11-10
occurrence.claim: On 2025-10-09 MOFCOM issued two decrees expanding export control over the rare-earth supply chain: Decree 61 covering foreign-made rare-earth metals and products, and Decree 62 covering rare-earth TECHNOLOGY including mining, smelting and separation, magnetic-material manufacturing and secondary-resource recycling, with 13 input materials, four permanent-magnet materials and seven target materials named; the measures were suspended from 2025-11-07 until 2026-11-10, making that date a scheduled forward event.

occurrence_strength.basis: Published decrees with numbers, a named scope and a dated suspension window, which makes 2026-11-10 a SCHEDULED occurrence in the method §0 sense and a forward-calendar entry regardless of disposition. Second dated item: CIRS Group on the temporary suspension until 2026-11-10, https://www.cirs-group.com/en/chemicals/china-temporarily-suspends-export-controls-on-key-raw-materials-including-rare-earths-lithium-batteries-and-diamond.

economic_impact.basis: Controls on rare-earth TECHNOLOGY, not just material, are the more consequential half: they constrain anyone trying to build separation or magnet-making capacity outside China, which is the entire premise of every ex-China magnet project.

unmappedness.basis: Lower than it looks. The material controls are exhaustively covered. The technology decree is less so, and the specific chain from a technology-transfer restriction to who can actually commission a separation train or a sintering line outside China is thinly mapped. But this is close to a saturated theme and the score reflects that.

public_market_reach.basis: The reachable non-miner positions are magnet makers, separation-equipment and chemical suppliers, and recyclers, most of which are small, private, or minor segments of larger companies. The retail-visible names are precisely the ones TASTE-001 refuses.

overlap.basis: No overlap with an existing card. Adjacent to CAND-20260830-06 (Niger uranium) as a second strategic-materials entry.
